A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chemical structure of neutral gas in low-metallicity galaxies is similar to that in the Galaxy.
the H2 and [ C II] emission is not affected by changes of the metallicity while the CO emission is affected.
the chemical structure of neutral molecular clouds in low-metal environments is very similar to that in the Galaxy, except that the clouds are smaller.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CO emission is an excellent indicator of the size of molecular clouds, while the [C II] and H2 emission are not.
CO emission from the surface of a cloud is not a good measure of the cloud size, and therefore the CO-to-H2 conversion factor should be used with caution in environments with low metallicity.
CO is a good tracer of dense gas, but that the CO emission can be optically thick, which can lead to an overestimate of the size of the CO-bearing cloud.
